scope: M6 runnable navigation examples; M2 and M5 remain deferred

reasons.Tabs: value/onChange and defaultValue are real ownership modes; no readOnly or validation API.
reasons.Breadcrumbs: BreadcrumbItem has no disabled field; empty items, long labels and keyboard links are meaningful cases.
reasons.menus: MenuItem disabled is real. DropdownMenu and ContextMenu own popup state internally; no open/defaultOpen, readOnly or validation interface.
reasons.appNavigation: Item arrays and active links are data-driven navigation, not dual-mode value inputs. All four exports have individual reachable examples.
reasons.AnchorNavigation: activeId/onNavigate is caller-owned. AnchorItem has no disabled field. Example navigation preserves the Explorer hash route.
reasons.CommandPalette: open/defaultOpen and query/defaultQuery are real modes; commands=[], loading and disabled command items are real states. Hook is demonstrated in a runnable owner.
reasons.Pagination: page/onPageChange is controlled-only. loadingPage/loadingPageSize, total=0 and custom summary use actual props; no readOnly or validation API.
reasons.Stepper: currentId/onStepChange is controlled. Omitting onStepChange renders noninteractive progress rather than a nonexistent readOnly prop. steps[].status=error is real error styling.
reasons.LoadMore: hasMore=false is the end state, not proof of empty data. Request failure belongs to the caller; there are no value ownership or validation modes.
reasons.InfiniteScroll: Uses the existing official LoadMore keyboard composition, preserving the deferred M5 policy. No fabricated empty/error/value modes.

limits: Applicability and structural fixtures do not certify browser behavior or accessibility.
The manifest contains ten navigation families, not the twelve suggested task labels; no nonexistent component or export was invented.
Root task owns execution evidence, metadata, live progress ledger and publication.
